scenarios.title: Three short
scenarios.when: Act 4 · Deputy whip · A minority government
scenarios.blurb: The budget is Thursday. The party that was propping the government up walked out of the deal on Friday. The count on your desk says the government loses by three.
scenarios.brief: {bill} comes to a vote on Thursday and it is confidence. {partner} tore up the agreement on Friday and every other bench is whipped against. The count this morning: {ours} for, {theirs} against, {short} short of carrying it. {away} You have four days, the pair book, the leave book and the bells.

outcomes.won: Carried by {margin}. The leader won't say thank you; the leader will say nothing at all, which is the same thing.
outcomes.lost: Lost by {margin}. A supply vote. The House has no confidence in the government, and the government, this morning, has none in its whips.
outcomes.noVote: Thursday came and went without the division. The budget sits on the Order Paper and so does the question of who let it slip.
outcomes.fell: The government fell. Nobody in the whip's office will say the word election out loud yet.

scenarios.title: The room turns
scenarios.blurb: Caucus meets at ten. There is a bill the benches hate, a ringleader with a list, and a leader who would rather it were your name on it than theirs.
scenarios.brief: {bill} is Thursday, whipped, and half the caucus has ridings that will hate them for it. {ringleader} has been round the lobbies since Monday with a list of names. Caucus is at ten. It isn't the leader they're after.

outcomes.held: You're still the whip. Some of the names on that list will need a reason to forget they signed it.
outcomes.ousted: The room turned and it took you with it. Whoever counts the votes on Thursday, it won't be you.
outcomes.noRevolt: The room grumbled and settled. Whatever was on the list stayed on it.

scenarios.title: Home truths
scenarios.when: Act 1 · Rookie · Your riding versus the line
scenarios.blurb: Thursday's bill does real harm to the people who sent you. The whip wants you in the lobby with the party. The riding association president wants a word.
scenarios.brief: {bill} is whipped {position} and comes to a vote on Thursday. At home it is the only thing anyone is talking about, and they are not talking about it kindly. Your mentor knows how this goes; the whip knows how it ends. Friday you go home either way.

outcomes.riding: You voted with the riding. Standing at home {standing}. The whip's office has a file with your name on it now, and a column marked useful trouble.
outcomes.party: You toed the line. Standing at home {standing}. The whip nodded once in the lobby, which from this whip is a parade.
outcomes.noVote: The vote never came. The riding is still waiting to find out who you are.
